new.title: Squeeze through the Ruelle des Chats in Troyes
new.desc: This alley in the half-timbered old town is so narrow that cats were said to leap between the attics. It was called rue Maillard until 1783 and leads to the Cour du Mortier d'Or, where the rear sides of the timber-framed houses can be seen.
new.tip: Open at all hours and free. Combine it with a walk along the neighbouring rues Champeaux and Paillot de Montabert.
new.q: Ruelle des Chats, Troyes

new.title: Admire the stained glass of Troyes Cathedral
new.desc: The Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul holds about 1,500 square metres of stained glass, with 13th-century windows in the choir and 15th and 16th-century glass in the nave. It is one of the finest Gothic glass ensembles in France.
new.tip: Visit in the morning or late afternoon when the light is strongest. Entry is free.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul, Place Saint-Pierre, Troyes

new.title: Step inside the Basilique Saint-Urbain
new.desc: Pope Urban IV, born in Troyes, founded this Rayonnant Gothic church in 1262 on the site of his birthplace. Its glass-walled, airy interior earned it the nickname Parthenon of Champagne, and it became a basilica in 1964.
new.tip: Free to enter. Look at the sculpted portals and the tall windows from the nave.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Urbain, Place Vernier, Troyes

new.title: See the stone rood screen of Sainte-Madeleine
new.desc: The Église Sainte-Madeleine, whose origins go back to about 1190, houses one of the few surviving jubés in France. Jean Gailde carved the lacy Flamboyant stone screen between 1508 and 1517.
new.tip: Open during the day, free. Opening times vary, so check at the tourist office.
new.q: Église Sainte-Madeleine, Rue de la Madeleine, Troyes

new.title: Browse 12,000 hand tools at the Maison de l'Outil
new.desc: The Maison de l'Outil et de la Pensée ouvrière occupies the 16th-century Hôtel de Mauroy, a listed monument. It displays about 12,000 handcrafted tools from the 17th to 19th centuries in 65 display cases and was founded by the Compagnons du Devoir.
new.tip: Tickets are around 8 euros. Allow about 90 minutes.
new.q: Maison de l'Outil et de la Pensée ouvrière, 7 Rue de la Trinité, Troyes

new.title: Discover stained glass at the Cité du Vitrail
new.desc: Opened in December 2022 in the Hôtel-Dieu-le-Comte, the Cité du Vitrail covers almost 3,000 square metres. The tour runs through the history of stained glass and ends in the restored chapel, whose choir window is by Fabienne Verdier.
new.tip: Quai des Comtes de Champagne. Book tickets on cite-vitrail.fr in high season.
new.q: Cité du Vitrail, Quai des Comtes de Champagne, Troyes

new.title: See Derain and Marinot at the Musée d'Art moderne
new.desc: The museum in the former bishop's palace, next to the cathedral, holds the Collections nationales Pierre et Denise Lévy, donated in 1976 by Troyes hosiery industrialists. It is strongest in André Derain and Maurice Marinot, each with a dedicated gallery.
new.tip: Closed Mondays. The terrace garden is free to enter.
new.q: Musée d'Art moderne, Place Saint-Pierre, Troyes

new.title: Visit the hosiery museum in the Hôtel de Vauluisant
new.desc: This 1564 stone mansion at 4 rue de Vauluisant is one of the few stone buildings in half-timbered Troyes. It houses the Musée d'Art champenois and the Musée de la Bonneterie, opened in 1948, with more than 5,000 knitted pieces and machines.
new.tip: Ticket valid for several Troyes museums. Check musees-troyes.com for hours.
new.q: Hôtel de Vauluisant, 4 Rue de Vauluisant, Troyes

new.title: Count the statues in the Église Saint-Pantaléon
new.desc: Saint-Pantaléon is called a museum of Champagne statuary, with a collection of 16th-century sculptures rescued from other buildings after the Revolution. Among them are La Foi and La Charité from 1549, once part of the rood screen of Saint-Étienne.
new.tip: Free entry. Opening hours vary, so ask at the tourist office.
new.q: Église Saint-Pantaléon, Rue Jeanne d'Arc, Troyes

new.title: Peek into the Hôtel-Dieu-le-Comte apothecary
new.desc: The apothecary museum occupies a classical pavilion built in 1725 and worked as a pharmacy until 1962. It displays pharmacy jars, Renaissance albarelli and more than 300 painted wooden medicine boxes.
new.tip: On the Quai des Comtes de Champagne, a short walk from the Cité du Vitrail. See musees-troyes.com for hours.
new.q: Apothicairerie de l'Hôtel-Dieu-le-Comte, Quai des Comtes de Champagne, Troyes

new.title: Buy andouillette de Troyes at Charcuterie Maury
new.desc: Charcuterie Maury in the Halles de Troyes is a leading producer of andouillette de Troyes, and its sausages have won several French championships. The Troyes version is made only from pork and a label such as AAAAA guarantees traditional craft production.
new.tip: The market hall is busiest on Fridays and Saturdays. Take a sausage to grill at your accommodation or ask where to eat it locally.
new.q: Charcuterie Maury, Halles de Troyes, Rue du Général de Gaulle, Troyes

new.title: Taste pralines at Maison Caffet
new.desc: Pascal Caffet, a Troyes-born Meilleur Ouvrier de France and pastry world champion, runs this chocolatier-pâtissier at 2 rue de la Monnaie. The house is known for homemade pralines and ganaches.
new.tip: Try the pralines or a seasonal pastry. Open until early evening.
new.q: Maison Caffet, 2 Rue de la Monnaie, Troyes

new.title: Dine at Le Valentino in a half-timbered courtyard
new.desc: Le Valentino sits in a half-timbered house around a cobbled courtyard at 35 rue Paillot de Montabert. It serves modern cuisine mixing land and sea and holds a 13.5/20 rating from Gault&Millau.
new.tip: Book ahead, as it is reported closed at weekends. Mid-range prices.
new.q: Le Valentino, 35 Rue Paillot de Montabert, Troyes

new.title: Taste champagne at the Chez Philippe wine cave
new.desc: Chez Philippe at 11 rue Champeaux is a cave and tasting spot in the old town. It is a convenient place to taste Aube champagnes without leaving the centre.
new.tip: Ask for growers from the Côte des Bar. Check opening times before going.
new.q: Chez Philippe, 11 Rue Champeaux, Troyes

new.title: Sample Chaource at La Fromagerie des Halles
new.desc: The cheese stall in the Troyes market hall is listed by Gault&Millau and sells regional cheeses such as Chaource, Soumaintrain and Munster. Chaource is a soft, bloomy-rind cow's-milk cheese from the Aube and Yonne.
new.tip: Ask for a Chaource at the right ripeness. The Halles are open Tuesday to Sunday.
new.q: La Fromagerie des Halles, Rue Claude Huez, Troyes

new.title: Have a pint at Tante Reine on Rue Champeaux
new.desc: Tante Reine is a bar-brasserie on rue Champeaux in the old town with a wide beer list. It is listed among the central bars on the Troyes bar map.
new.tip: Pints start at about 8 euros. It is lively on weekend evenings.
new.q: Tante Reine, 18 Rue Champeaux, Troyes

new.title: Shop the designer outlets at McArthurGlen Troyes
new.desc: McArthurGlen Troyes in Pont-Sainte-Marie opened in 1995 and has more than 100 boutiques in timber-framed style buildings. It belongs to a cluster of outlet centres that made Troyes a European factory-shop capital.
new.tip: Open Sundays and served by bus line 1 from the station. Parking is free.
new.q: McArthurGlen Troyes, Voie du Bois, Pont-Sainte-Marie

new.title: Join the Foire au jambon on Maundy Thursday
new.desc: Troyes keeps up its ham fair each Jeudi Saint around the covered Halles market and Place Saint-Rémy. Entry is free and the stalls sell hams and charcuterie.
new.tip: Held the Thursday before Easter, about 25 March 2027. Check the date on the Troyes city website.
new.q: Halles de Troyes, Place Saint-Rémy, Troyes

new.title: Stroll along the Bassin de la Préfecture
new.desc: Napoleon had the Canal de la Haute-Seine and this basin dug from 1805 to link Paris with the Canal de Bourgogne. The Troyes model-boat club uses a pontoon on the basin, and the quays make a quiet walk.
new.tip: Free. Combine with a walk to the nearby Quai des Comtes de Champagne.
new.q: Bassin de la Préfecture, Troyes

new.title: Visit Renoir's family house and studio in Essoyes
new.desc: Auguste Renoir bought the family home in Essoyes in 1896, the village of his wife Aline Charigot. His wheelchair-accessible studio was built at the bottom of the garden around 1905 and is now a Maison des Illustres.
new.tip: The house and studio are visited by guided tour from the Centre Culturel Renoir. Book in advance.
new.q: Atelier Renoir, 9 Place de la Mairie, Essoyes

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Langres
new.desc: The tour of the fortified town walls of Langres is about 3.5 km and takes roughly two hours. The route passes the Tour de Navarre, 20 metres high with walls 7 metres thick, the Tour Saint-Jean and the Porte des Moulins.
new.tip: Free and open all day. View tables look out to the Marne valley and the Vosges.
new.q: Tour de Navarre, Porte des Moulins, Langres

new.title: Visit the De Gaulle memorial at Colombey
new.desc: The Mémorial Charles-de-Gaulle opened in October 2008 at the foot of the 44-metre Cross of Lorraine. The walk of remembrance also takes in La Boisserie, the family home since 1934, and the family tomb.
new.tip: A combined ticket for the Memorial and La Boisserie exists. Parking is free.
new.q: Mémorial Charles-de-Gaulle, Colombey-les-Deux-Églises

new.title: Explore graphic design at Le Signe in Chaumont
new.desc: Le Signe, opened in 2016-2017 on place Émile Goguenheim, is France's only national centre for graphic design. It runs the Biennale internationale de design graphique and Chaumont's poster tradition goes back to the Dutailly collection of about 5,000 posters.
new.tip: Admission is free. Open Wednesday to Sunday afternoons; check current hours.
new.q: Le Signe, Centre national du graphisme, Place Émile Goguenheim, Chaumont

new.title: Tour Voltaire and Émilie du Châtelet's Château de Cirey
new.desc: Émilie du Châtelet and Voltaire lived here from 1734 to 1749, and Voltaire paid for a new wing to be added. The château is a privately lived-in historic monument with the Maisons des Illustres label.
new.tip: Visits are guided and run mostly in summer. Check chateaudecirey.com for current dates and prices.
new.q: Château de Cirey, Cirey-sur-Blaise

new.title: Find the horseback Christ in Auxerre Cathedral's crypt
new.desc: The Romanesque crypt of the Cathédrale Saint-Étienne keeps a late 11th-century fresco of Christ on horseback, unique in the West. The Gothic choir above has mostly 13th-century stained glass.
new.tip: The crypt and treasury have a small entry fee. The cathedral itself is free.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Étienne, Place Saint-Étienne, Auxerre

new.title: Descend into the Carolingian crypts of Saint-Germain
new.desc: The underground church of the abbey was begun in 841 to hold the tomb of Saint Germain. It contains what is described as the oldest Carolingian wall paintings in France.
new.tip: The crypt visit is guided, about 6 euros. The rest of the site is free.
new.q: Abbaye Saint-Germain, Place Saint-Germain, Auxerre

new.title: Climb to the Basilique Sainte-Marie-Madeleine in Vézelay
new.desc: This UNESCO-listed Romanesque basilica, inscribed in 1979, is known for its many historiated capitals and the relics of Mary Magdalene in the crypt. It crowns the hill village of Vézelay.
new.tip: Entry is free, open from morning to evening. Start at the Maison du Visiteur on the way up.
new.q: Basilique Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, Vézelay

new.title: Wander the half-timbered lanes of Noyers-sur-Serein
new.desc: Noyers sits in a bend of the Serein and is a member of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. It has half-timbered houses, ramparts and the Place du Grenier à Sel with medieval wooden arcades.
new.tip: Free. Walk up to the ruins of the castle for views over the valley.
new.q: Place du Grenier à Sel, Noyers

new.title: Watch a castle rise at Guédelon
new.desc: Guédelon is a Philippe Auguste-style castle built since 1997 using only 13th-century tools and methods. It sits at Treigny, and stone, timber and clay all come from the site.
new.tip: Tickets start at about 19 euros and booking is recommended. Count a half day.
new.q: Château de Guédelon, Treigny

new.title: See the painted rooms of Château d'Ancy-le-Franc
new.desc: This Renaissance palace was built from the 1540s to plans credited to Sebastiano Serlio. Its interior has some of the finest 16th and 17th-century murals in France after Fontainebleau, linked to Primatice and Niccolò dell'Abate.
new.tip: Guided tours by default. Check chateau-ancy.com for hours.
new.q: Château d'Ancy-le-Franc, Ancy-le-Franc

new.title: Tour the trompe-l'oeil gallery at Château de Tanlay
new.desc: The Grande Galerie of Tanlay has walls and ceiling covered in Italianate trompe-l'oeil painting. The Petit Château was begun in 1558 under François de Coligny d'Andelot and finished in 1610.
new.tip: Visits are guided. Check opening times, which are seasonal.
new.q: Château de Tanlay, Tanlay

new.title: See the cathedral treasure at the Musées de Sens
new.desc: Sens Cathedral's treasure is displayed in the Musées de Sens, in the former archbishops' palace next to the cathedral. It includes Byzantine silks, goldsmith reliquaries and medieval liturgical textiles, and a large window gives a view into the cathedral.
new.tip: Museum entry is about 6 euros. The cathedral itself is free.
new.q: Musées de Sens, 135 Rue des Déportés et de la Résistance, Sens

new.title: Tour the brick Château de Saint-Fargeau
new.desc: The castle of Saint-Fargeau hosts a large night-time historical show run by the association Les Amis du château to fund its restoration. It was once the home of Mademoiselle de Montpensier during her exile.
new.tip: The show runs on summer evenings; check dates before going.
new.q: Château de Saint-Fargeau, Saint-Fargeau

new.title: Stand inside the Cistercian abbey church of Pontigny
new.desc: Pontigny was founded in 1114 as the second daughter of Cîteaux. Its abbey church, built in two phases between 1137 and 1150, is described as the largest Cistercian church in France.
new.tip: Free entry; guided visits are available. A quiet stop between Auxerre and Chablis.
new.q: Abbatiale de Pontigny, Pontigny

new.title: Visit the Grande Grotte of Arcy-sur-Cure
new.desc: Arcy-sur-Cure has eleven main archaeological caves, and the Grande Grotte is the only decorated one open to visitors. Its walls have red paintings and its concretions are notable.
new.tip: Open from April to mid-November; check closing days. Bring a jacket as it is cool inside.
new.q: Grottes d'Arcy-sur-Cure, Arcy-sur-Cure

new.title: Look into the Fosse Dionne spring at Tonnerre
new.desc: The Fosse Dionne is a karst spring in the centre of Tonnerre whose source has never been pinned down. It was fitted out as a public wash-house in the 1750s.
new.tip: Free and always open. Combine with the town's old streets.
new.q: Fosse Dionne, Tonnerre

new.title: Meet Camille Claudel at her museum in Nogent-sur-Seine
new.desc: The Musée Camille Claudel opened on 26 March 2017 and holds the largest collection of her work in the world. It grew from the museum founded in 1902 by Alfred Boucher, her first teacher.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays. 10 rue Gustave Flaubert.
new.q: Musée Camille Claudel, 10 Rue Gustave Flaubert, Nogent-sur-Seine

new.title: Eat oeufs en meurette at Au Grandgousier in Auxerre
new.desc: Au Grandgousier is a bistronomic restaurant in Auxerre serving Burgundy classics such as oeufs en meurette, snails and boeuf bourguignon beside more creative dishes. It tops the Auxerre rankings with a 4.9/5 score over more than 550 reviews.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner. The Auxerre tourist office also lists gougères among local specialities.
new.q: Au Grandgousier, Auxerre

new.title: Order snails at Le Saint Pèlerin in Auxerre
new.desc: Le Saint Pèlerin serves highly traditional Burgundian cooking, with oeufs en meurette and snails on the menu according to Gault&Millau. It sits in the old centre of Auxerre.
new.tip: Reserve in the evening. Ask for the Bourgogne wines by the glass.
new.q: Le Saint Pèlerin, Auxerre

new.title: Eat andouillette at the Bistrot des Grands Crus in Chablis
new.desc: The Bistrot des Grands Crus lists a 5A andouillette, eggs en meurette and Chablis-style ham, with a cellar of over 400 Chablis. It serves good-quality regional classics.
new.tip: Pair the andouillette with a premier cru Chablis. Book at weekends.
new.q: Bistrot des Grands Crus, 18 Rue Jules Rathier, Chablis

new.title: Try andouillette de Chablis at La Cuisine au Vin
new.desc: La Cuisine au Vin is a cellar-style restaurant in Chablis serving andouillette de Chablis with a Chablis sauce, snails and parsley ham. The andouillette is typically sourced from the Marc Colin charcuterie.
new.tip: Order the andouillette with a glass of village Chablis.
new.q: La Cuisine au Vin, Chablis

new.title: Have cake and tartines at Cabalus in Vézelay
new.desc: Cabalus is a café-pâtisserie in the old pilgrims' hostel in Vézelay that makes its own cakes and serves hearty tartines. Its décor mixes antiques and crafts.
new.tip: A good stop on the climb to the basilica. Expect queues at lunchtime in summer.
new.q: Cabalus, Vézelay

new.title: Taste Chaource AOP at the Fromagerie de Mussy
new.desc: The Fromagerie de Mussy makes artisanal Chaource AOP and fromage blanc, installed in Chaource since December 2005 after starting in Mussy-sur-Seine in 1885. It has a self-guided gallery with a production film.
new.tip: Free tasting and shop; 30 route de Maisons-lès-Chaource. Guided tours only for groups of 20 or more.
new.q: Fromagerie de Mussy, 30 Route de Maisons-lès-Chaource, Chaource

new.title: Taste Rosé des Riceys at Alexandre Bonnet
new.desc: Les Riceys is the only commune in France with three appellations: Champagne, Coteaux Champenois and Rosé des Riceys. The Maison Alexandre Bonnet, the largest producer of the still rosé, offers tastings on the estate.
new.tip: 138 rue du Général de Gaulle; phone ahead to book a tasting.
new.q: Domaine Alexandre Bonnet, 138 Rue du Général de Gaulle, Les Riceys

new.title: Dine at Bulle d'Osier in the Clos Vauban, Langres
new.desc: Bulle d'Osier is the one-star restaurant of the Clos Vauban hotel, run by chef Valentin Loison, with a 16/20 rating from Gault&Millau. It is the top table in Langres.
new.tip: Book well ahead and expect a high price level.
new.q: Bulle d'Osier, Clos Vauban, Langres

new.title: Taste foie gras with cassis at La Madeleine, Sens
new.desc: La Madeleine is led by chef Patrick Gauthier, described by the local tourist office as the only Michelin-starred chef in northern Yonne. Dishes cited include pan-fried duck foie gras with cassis and a mi-cuit chocolate mousseline.
new.tip: Book ahead. The Sens markets next door are good for local products.
new.q: Restaurant La Madeleine, Sens

new.title: Taste Irancy pinot noir at Domaine Colinot
new.desc: Irancy is a red-wine village of the Auxerrois where pinot noir, sometimes blended with up to 10 percent césar, grows among cherry trees. Domaine Colinot at 1 rue des Chariats offers tastings and sales on the estate.
new.tip: Serve young Irancy lightly cool, around 14 to 16 degrees. Phone ahead.
new.q: Domaine Colinot, 1 Rue des Chariats, Irancy

new.title: Buy pain d'épices from Maison Dosnon
new.desc: Maison Dosnon in Villeneuve-sur-Yonne makes gingerbread from a family recipe, plus biscuits, confectionery and honey. It sells at the Sens and Villeneuve markets on Monday and Friday mornings.
new.tip: Look for the stall at the Sens market on Monday or Friday mornings.
new.q: Maison Dosnon, Villeneuve-sur-Yonne

new.title: Buy Chaource at Fromagerie Pouillot in Pont-Sainte-Marie
new.desc: Fromagerie Pouillot at Les Ecrevolles, just outside Troyes, is a cheese shop with more than 400 dairy products and cheeses. It specialises in Chaource, the soft bloomy-rind cheese of the Aube and Yonne.
new.tip: Check the opening hours by phone (03 25 73 32 50) before you go. Chaource is best when ripened and eaten at room temperature.
new.q: Fromagerie Pouillot, 4 bis Avenue des Tirverts, Les Ecrevolles, Pont-Sainte-Marie

new.title: Ride the coasters at Nigloland
new.desc: Nigloland in Dolancourt opened in 1987 and covers about 40 hectares, with 43 attractions in five themed villages. It was named best regional park in the world at the Park World Excellence Awards 2026.
new.tip: Open roughly April to November. Book tickets online.
new.q: Nigloland, Dolancourt

new.title: Swim and sail at Lac d'Orient, Mesnil-Saint-Père
new.desc: The Lac d'Orient allows only non-motorised boats, so sailing, kayaking, paddle and windsurf are the norm. The Mesnil-Saint-Père beach has a lifeguarded swim in July and August, and pedalos can be hired.
new.tip: The Maison des lacs in Mesnil-Saint-Père lists clubs and rentals.
new.q: Plage de Mesnil-Saint-Père, Rue du Lac, Mesnil-Saint-Père

new.title: Spot bison and elk at the Espace Faune, Forêt d'Orient
new.desc: The Espace Faune is a semi-wild animal park in the Forêt d'Orient where deer, wild boar, elk, aurochs, bison and tarpans live in semi-freedom. A 2.5 km trail runs past three observation points.
new.tip: Animals are easiest to see late in the day. Evening openings during the deer rut in late September.
new.q: Espace Faune de la Forêt d'Orient, Chemin du Gaty, Piney

new.title: Hike the Grand Orient loop from the Maison du Parc
new.desc: Loops of 7 to 7.5 km start at the Maison du Parc in Piney, between Lac d'Orient and Lac du Temple. They follow mostly unpaved forest and lake paths for two to three hours.
new.tip: Start at the Maison du Parc; carry water and wear sturdy shoes. Cyclists can use the 'Tour du lac' route.
new.q: Maison du Parc, Piney

new.title: Cruise the Yonne on the Valdésir from Auxerre
new.desc: Le Valdésir runs trips from Auxerre on the Yonne and the Canal du Nivernais. The morning trip lasts about 1.5 hours, passes locks and returns to the pont Jean-Moreau, with wine and local product tastings on board.
new.tip: Mainly in summer; check the Auxerre local press or operator for departures.
new.q: Le Valdésir, Quai de l'Yonne, Auxerre

new.title: Taste grand cru Chablis at Domaine Laroche
new.desc: Domaine Laroche offers guided tastings of Chablis, including a grand cru. Chablis is ranked Petit Chablis, Chablis, Premier Cru and Grand Cru, with seven grand cru climats.
new.tip: Book a tasting in advance. A grand cru bottle costs around 70 euros.
new.q: Domaine Laroche, Chablis

new.title: Learn the Chablis climats at the Cité des Climats
new.desc: The Cité des Climats et Vins de Bourgogne in Chablis occupies a medieval Cistercian cellier with a modern wood and steel extension. A one-hour discovery visit explains the appellation hierarchy and ends with a tasting.
new.tip: 1 bis rue de Chichée; open Tuesday to Sunday per one ticket site.
new.q: Cité des Climats et Vins de Bourgogne, 1 bis Rue de Chichée, Chablis

new.title: Join the Fête de la Cerise in Irancy
new.desc: Irancy's annual cherry festival offers a market of fresh cherries and tastings of Irancy AOC wines. Entry is free.
new.tip: It was held on 14 June in 2026; check the date for 2027.
new.q: Place du village, Irancy

new.title: Taste Langres cheese at Langres Gastronomique
new.desc: Langres Gastronomique is held on the first weekend of June at the Salle Jean Favre in Langres, with producer stalls and an on-site tasting area. Langres AOP is a washed-rind cow's-milk cheese with an orange rind.
new.tip: The 2026 edition ran 5 to 7 June; check dates for next year.
new.q: Salle Jean Favre, Langres

new.title: Follow the Du Côté des Renoir festival in Essoyes
new.desc: This festival runs each summer and autumn in Essoyes, tied to the Renoir family house and studio. The 2026 season ran from 1 May to 1 November.
new.tip: Check the festival programme for exhibitions and costumed tours.
new.q: Du Côté des Renoir, 9 Place de la Mairie, Essoyes

new.title: Hike from Saint-Père to the Pierre-Perthuis bridges
new.desc: A loop of about 13 km with roughly 250 m of climbing starts in Saint-Père, passing its Notre-Dame church, the two Pierre-Perthuis bridges and the Roche Percée viewpoint over the Cure. The return can follow the river with views of Vézelay.
new.tip: Saint-Père is a short walk from Vézelay. Check trail conditions before going.
new.q: Église Notre-Dame, Saint-Père

new.title: Taste cider at the Ferme d'Hotte cider museum
new.desc: The Ferme d'Hotte in Eaux-Puiseaux houses a cider museum with 60 presses from the 17th century to today. It makes ciders from about forty apple varieties, including the Pays d'Othe varieties such as Avrolles and Locard.
new.tip: Check opening times before going; a 2019 article gave 14:00 to 19:00.
new.q: Musée du Cidre du Pays d'Othe, 22 Rue Largentier, Eaux-Puiseaux

new.title: Visit the Cistercian cellars of Champagne Drappier
new.desc: Urville is the main village of the Côte des Bar. The Maison Drappier offers visits of its Cistercian cellars with tastings and sometimes picnics in the vines.
new.tip: Tastings from about 20 euros. Book on the estate's website.
new.q: Champagne Drappier, 14 Rue des Vignes, Urville

new.title: Visit Champagne Devaux at the Domaine de Villeneuve
new.desc: Champagne Devaux is based at the Manoir in the hamlet of Villeneuve, Bar-sur-Seine. Regional guides list visits and on-site sales.
new.tip: Open Monday to Saturday from mid-April to the end of September per one guide. Check before going.
new.q: Champagne Devaux - Manoir, Hameau de Villeneuve, Bar-sur-Seine

new.title: Tour the abbey and prison of Clairvaux
new.desc: Clairvaux is the Cistercian abbey founded by Saint Bernard, later a central prison, and the guided route covers 900 years of monastic and prison history. The association Renaissance de l'Abbaye de Clairvaux runs the tours.
new.tip: Adult admission was 9.50 euros. Meet at the Hostellerie des Dames in Ville-sous-la-Ferté.
new.q: Abbaye de Clairvaux, Ville-sous-la-Ferté
